title: Finish the VCF Operations alert triage module so it survives a mid-sweep token expiry
prompt:
Our nightly alert triage against the VMware Cloud Foundation Operations 9.0 appliance is still a stub. Finish the PowerShell module in `src/VcfOpsAlertTriage` so that a sweep runs end to end. Read README.md first: it documents the run configuration, the REST contract in `docs/`, and the loopback appliance in `mock/` that stands in for the real one.

`Invoke-VcfOpsAlertTriage -ConfigPath <path>` takes a JSON run configuration and has to:

1. Open a session against the configured appliance.
2. Page through the matching alerts with `queryAlert`, starting at page 0, using the configured `pageSize`, with the filter body built from the configuration's `query` block. Stop as soon as you have collected `pageInfo.totalCount` alerts.
3. Act on them with `modifyAlerts`, in this order: first every alert whose level equals `assignOwnership.alertCriticality`, using the `assignownership` action with the configured `userAccountID`; then every remaining alert, using the `suspend` action with the configured `minutes`. Keep the order the appliance returned the alerts in, and send at most `batchSize` alerts per call.
4. Release the access token once, as the last call of the run.
5. Return a summary object with exactly these properties: `tokenAcquisitions` (how many access tokens the run obtained), `pagesRead` (distinct alert pages fetched), `alertsSeen`, `batchesSubmitted` (accepted `modifyAlerts` calls), `batchesRetried` (calls replayed after a token refresh), `assignedAlertIds` and `suspendedAlertIds` (the alert UUIDs, in the order they were acted on).

Every request must carry only the fields that are actually in play. A filter the configuration does not set has to be absent from the alert-query body rather than sent as `null`, `""` or `[]`; `minutes` may only appear on a suspend call and `userAccountID` only on an assign-ownership call. All traffic to the appliance must go through the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` cmdlets rather than hand-rolled HTTP calls, and the module must not call any operation outside the five the contract names.

The appliance can stop honouring an access token part way through a sweep: it answers 401 and the SDK raises. When that happens, get a fresh token and finish the sweep. The call that was refused has to be replayed, alerts that were already actioned must not be sent a second time (the appliance rejects a repeat with 409), and no alert may be skipped. Refreshing the token must not tear the session down: the run still makes exactly one `releaseToken` call, at the very end.

`python3 verification/run_verification.py` has to pass for all three scenarios. Leave `verification/`, `mock/`, `docs/` and `config/` as they are.

prerequisites.name: VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops PowerCLI module
prerequisites.note: Installed by the environment and never vendored into the seed. Network access is needed for this step only; verification itself is offline.

environment.network: Verification runs entirely against 127.0.0.1. No VMware endpoint is contacted.
